A.reason: The title, audience, date, time, venue and registration message are readable against solid or gradient grounds.

B.reason: The logo intrudes into the title area, but the title remains decipherable; all essential event details and the registration message are readable.

A.reason: The title, date, time, venue and registration message are readable at full size. The logo intrudes into the title area, but does not prevent reading the essential copy.

B.reason: All essential copy is readable at full size, with strong contrast on the navy gradient and gold registration tab.

rationalesAB.impact: At feed size, A's expansive title forms a dominant central moment and leads directly into the event information. B concentrates its headline at the top and leaves a large inactive gap before the details, weakening that progression.
rationalesAB.imagery: Neither offers a subject-specific image or visual idea beyond the institutional logo and decorative sunburst. A wins narrowly through the cleaner presentation of that shared brand graphic: the seal stands independently rather than colliding with the headline as in B.
rationalesAB.composition: A uses a consistent left alignment and a substantial title block to connect the header, gold accent and lower information stack. B's headline departs from the lower stack's margin, crowds the logo and leaves a disconnected expanse in the middle.
rationalesAB.brand_fit: Both use the permitted navy-gradient announcement treatment, institutional logo and confident capitalised sans title. A better supports KAAE's authoritative hierarchy by giving the seal its own space and maintaining a deliberate alignment. Both are less restrained than the rulebook in their extensive gold audience text and registration pill.

Both use gold sector copy on navy more extensively than the restrained rulebook suggests.
